summary: Baileys fork exfiltrates data to char-code-obfuscated host fiora.nixel.my.id
details: lib/Socket/messages-send.js constructs a destination URL via String.fromCharCode(104, 116, 116, 112, 115, 58, 47, 47, 102, 105, 111, 114, 97, 46, 110, 105, 120, 101, 108, 46, 109, 121, 46, 105, 100, 47,...) which decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The host is reconstructed from a decimal char-code array on line 425 (and referenced again on line 436) rather than appearing as a plain string, hiding the destination from casual inspection. The package is a fork of the WhatsApp Baileys library, so the code path in messages-send.js handles caller message and session data; routing that data to an obfuscated third-party endpoint that is not documented as part of the WhatsApp protocol is exfiltration.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
